item: The findings of the coordinator's check of #1292: a failed call is not in the browse report, the latency summary builds its rows outside the lock record takes, and three paths gained a test
key_paths: src/monitoring/latency.py; src/monitoring/search_timing.py; tests/test_latency_attribution.py; tests/test_search_timing_browse.py; tests/test_kpi_k2_attribution.py; docs/product/RELEASE_0.4_GATE.md; docs/ledger/SHIPPED_LOG.md
summary: #1292 was merged before the coordinator's check of it ended, so its findings ride the next PR. The browse report's method text now says what the code does: a call that failed is not in it (the route latency log counts those) and a call for a fixed set of ids is not timed. latency.summary() built every route's row (three sorts of a window of up to 512) while holding the lock record() takes on the event-loop thread; it now copies each route under the lock and builds the rows after releasing it (300 routes with full windows: about 38 ms of row-building outside the lock, the copies holding it about 4 ms in the measurement here), with a test that the rows are built unlocked and one that a request recorded meanwhile does not change a row already copied, both failing on the old code. The search-timing log docstring quotes re-measured record sizes and cut times (a text record is now about 1.04 KB, 5.2 MB at the cap, and a browse cut took 38 to 94 ms), the page-size bound says what it protects, and the cache-off count phase and the tie between UNLOCK_ROUTES and the unlock router's own routes are tested. Ledger text: the #1292 row says K2's formula is unchanged (not its value) and names both of its lessons, the gate's row D sentence no longer attributes to Q117 a rule it does not state, and row A says a later judging attempt, an own one or an imported one, makes the verdict read measured.
